doc.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

title: Every human is a musician; music as God's will
summary: He says all are musicians, music is God's will, and recalls buying his first drums by shining shoes.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Well I believe that every living human being is a musician. Some are learned and some are not. Those who are learned become fantastic musicians. They become players. Then there are those who become fantastic listeners, which — you can’t tell anyone how to listen to music. But you can tell someone how to play or how you would like them to play, but you can’t tell them how to listen to music. So in order to listen to music, that calls for some musicianship. This is an innate thing that we all are all blessed with. Because I believe that music is one of God’s wills and God’s will will be done. You can quote me on that.
It’s a good quote. A spiritual aspect of the craft, has that always been with you?

I think so, I think so. Because it’s just through the grace of God, man, that I’m even here today. Even as a kid coming up, I used to shine shoes with a shoeshine box to make enough money so that — I bought my first set of drums shining shoes. So that was helpful from the man upstairs. And I sincerely believe that it is God’s will about music. Because also there’s no anger in music. There’s no prejudice in music. So it’s got to be — something’s got to be happening. As a matter of fact, can you imagine what this world would be like without music?
No. I wouldn’t want to think about that.
